title: VH-3D Presidential Helicopter Pilot Qualified (I) (Col to Capt) NMOS (7532, 7562, 7563, 7564, 7565, 7566, 8042), DC AVN
raw_text:
46. MOS 7571, VH-3D Presidential Helicopter Pilot Qualified (I) (Col to
Capt) NMOS (7532, 7562, 7563, 7564, 7565, 7566, 8042), DC AVN

    a. Summary. White House Helicopter Aircraft Commanders (WHHAC) who
operate HMX-1 Marine VH-3D helicopters in support of the White House Military
Office (WHMO).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Security requirement:

                (a) Top secret security clearance eligibility.

                (b) Yankee White (YW) clearance eligibility.

            (3) Must be selected for assignment to HMX-1.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Pilot VH-3D qualified.

            (2) Qualified in a primary MOS from OccFld 75 or 8042.

        (3) Complete VH-3D White House Aircraft Commander's Syllabus in
accordance with HMX-1 VH-3D Aviation Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

        (4) Designated a White House Helicopter Aircraft Commander (WHHAC) by
the HMX-1 Commanding Officer.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the VH-
3D and VH-60N Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers 53-2011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators.
